description.narrative: The most significant project-level outcomes are economy-wide benefits through increased employment and value addition, and GHG emissions reduction. The Project will contribute to increasing domestic value addition in Indias specialty chemical sector through production of downstream and value-added products. The most significant effect of the Project on the market is through its scale expansion, backward integration, and the Companys drive to push innovation through manufacturing of products that are currently imported. The Project is also expected to achieve reduction in total GHG emissions through a combination of measures including partial coal replacement with biomass; increase in share of renewable power in energy mix and increase in waste heat utilization.

The proposed IFC investment involves a 10-year senior secured loan of up to US$130 million to Aarti Industries Limited (the Company or AIL). The proposed loan will be utilized towards capacity expansion, modernisation and debottlenecking initiatives (the Project) in Jhagadia and Dahej, in the state of Gujarat, India, which consists of: (i) expansion of nitro toluene capacities at Jhagadia, (ii) expansion of ethylation capacities at Dahej, (iii) setting up of a chloro-toluene and its derivatives plant at Jhagadia, (iv) setting up of multi-purpose plants and pilot plants for customized manufacturing at Jhagadia, and (v) expansion and debottlenecking of other existing capacities at Jhagadia and Dahej. IFCs loan is structured as a Sustainability Linked Loan (SLL) and builds in incentives for the Company to meet agreed emission reduction targets.
